summary: Deep technical discussion focused on tradeoffs between Redwood Hosted API and Dedicated private pools for BlueMesa's low-latency inference. Key topics: noisy neighbor mitigation, guaranteed throughput, KV cache behavior under shard/rollout, batching strategies, int8/4-bit quantization impacts, and VPC/on-prem constraints.
topics: Throughput guarantees vs. cost: reserved capacity SLAs
KV cache hit/miss accounting and prefix caching
Quantization tradeoffs (int8 vs int4) on quality and perf
VPC / on-prem considerations for private deployments
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We're gonna do a pretty technical deep-dive today, mainly around your latency hotspots and how Dedicated pools would behave versus Hosted. Samira will run through runtime stuff.
[00:12] Ravi (Customer): Yep thanks, we care about 50ms p50 for our short prompts and steady throughput at 1.2k qps during peak. Also worried about noisy neighbors when we share GPUs.
[00:24] Samira (SE): cool, so a few quick framing q's — are most requests short (<=512 tokens) or do you have a long-tail?
[00:31] Tasha: Mostly short, but we have a ~10% tail >2k tokens for batch scoring.
[00:37] Samira: okay that changes batching profiles; batching can help cost but for p50 latency you want small max batch windows. We profiled that on Hosted with continuous batching and got average token latencies down but p50s can degrade under noisy workloads.
[00:55] Miguel: when you say noisy neighbor what exactly happens? We've had one tenant spike and our p99 doubled.
[01:02] Samira: right — on shared hosts you can see cross-tenant interference at scheduling, kernel contention, memory bus. Redwood's hosted has soft isolation with weighted routing, but Dedicated gives you hard isolation (you get the pool). The trade is cost vs utilization efficiency.
[01:19] Jordan: to add — Dedicated supports reserved GPU pools and autoscaling policies, so you get throughput headroom guarantees up to your reserved capacity. We can set burst policies too.
[01:28] Ravi: is throughput guaranteed? e.g., can you promise X tokens/sec?
[01:31] Evan (Solutions Eng): we don't SLA per-token throughput for hosted, but for Dedicated we include throughput commitments in contracts — effectively you get predictable vGPU availability and we measure by p50 and sustained tokens/sec. The bench we run will produce a numbers sheet.
[01:44] Tasha: curious about KV cache — our application depends heavily on prefix caching for long conversations. If we move to Dedicated, is KV cache local to the pool?
[01:52] Samira: yes KV cache is per model shard/serving instance. On Dedicated it's within your pool, so cache affinity stays high. On Hosted we have a multi-tenant KV layer with smarter eviction; cold misses can route to regional fallback. Note: sometimes transcripts show 'K V' or 'K-V' in logs, so there can be naming mismatches in dashboards.
[02:10] Ravi: how do you measure KV hit/miss in benchmarks?
[02:14] Samira: we instrument hit-rate, latency delta on hit vs miss, and token savings. In the run I'll include a breakdown: cold start (empty cache), warm start with synthetic prefixes, and mixed traffic to emulate your 10% long-tail.
[02:25] Miguel: is there any chance cache thrashing across models or tenants?
[02:28] Samira: on Dedicated less likely; on Hosted eviction policies can cause thrash under high cardinality. We also implement prefix hashing to reduce collision but it's not perfect.
[02:40] Jordan: another lever is compilation and kernel selection. For shorter sequences we pick kernels optimized for memory locality vs long sequences which use different attention kernels, that affects throughput.
[02:52] Tasha: quantization — we tested int8 earlier and saw a small drop in nll but big perf gains. What's your recommendation?
[02:59] Evan: quantization is workload dependent. For generative quality-sensitive flows we suggest int8 calibrated with your eval set; for pure ranking/embedding tasks int4 can be fine. We'll include a quality regression delta in the bench. Beware int4 can change distribution of logits and sometimes hallucination patterns.
[03:18] Ravi: any issues running quantized models on on-prem vs cloud GPUs?
[03:21] Samira: depends on drivers and CUDA/ROCm builds. Our runtime picks kernels based on architecture and detects quantized-friendly paths. On-prem you may need specific driver minimums; we'll give a compatibility matrix.
[03:33] Tasha: batching strategies — we worry about tail latency if batching waits too long for batch fill.
[03:38] Samira: we use adaptive batch windows: preference for latency SLOs, fallback to throughput batching when underutilized. You can configure max wait (ms) and max batch size. For BlueMesa's 50ms p50 target you likely want max-wait around 6-8ms and small max-batch like 8-16 for short inputs.
[03:55] Miguel: if we run Dedicated and autoscale, will cache warmup cause spikes?
[04:00] Samira: yes newly provisioned replicas start cold; we have warmup strategies: background prefetch (proactive KV seeding) and sticky routing to keep hot shards warm. We'll simulate autoscale scenarios in the bench.
[04:12] Ravi: what's the instrumentation we get? Can we see token-level breakdowns and per-route latency?
[04:17] Jordan: Redwood Console exposes per-route token cost, latency histograms, and KV hit/miss counts. We'll give you access to a sample dashboard; note names can differ (e.g., "kv_hit" vs "cache_hit").
[04:26] Tasha: Security — on-prem deployment we'd need KMS/HSM integration and audit logs. How mature is that flow?
[04:31] Jordan: mature — Private deployments support customer-managed KMS, HSM integrations, and a private control plane. We'll send the security playbook and SOC2 artifacts.
[04:39] Miguel: any gotchas for VPC peering or egress?
[04:42] Evan: typically network egress must be allowed for health checks; on air-gapped options we bundle a local control plane image. We'll include network diagrams.
[04:49] Ravi: curious about failure modes — if one GPU in the dedicated pool dies, how does routing behave?
[04:54] Samira: the serving layer will detect unhealthy nodes and re-route; we keep KV replication per pool to reduce misses, but a sudden loss can cause brief p99 spikes while the pool rebuilds. We support rolling replacements to minimize full-pool impact.
[05:07] Tasha: what about multi-model serving? We run 3 model families. Can they share a dedicated pool?
[05:12] Evan: yes, but that introduces contention; best practice is isolated pools per critical family or scheduling weights so high-priority models get reserved capacity.
[05:22] Jordan: ok let's talk concrete bench we propose: two phases — 1) short prompt (<=512 tokens) high qps steady state to measure p50/p90/p99 and throughput; 2) mixed-tail with 10% long prompts to measure KV and tail effects. We'll include quantized vs fp16 comparisons.
[05:38] Ravi: can you surface the raw profiles like GPU util, kernel times? We want kernel-level breakdowns for us to compare to our profiler.
[05:45] Samira: yes; we will include per-step kernel timing, nvprof-esque metrics, and per-request trace ids. Note that some kernel names are vendor-specific and may appear different.
[05:56] Miguel: latency budgeting — we need an SLO doc.
[05:59] Jordan: we'll create a suggested SLO matrix based on your traffic: target p50 50ms, p90 120ms, p99 320ms for short prompts; we'll recommend capacity buffers and batching config.
[06:12] Tasha: what's the expected cost delta moving from Hosted to Dedicated for our profile? Rough estimate fine.
[06:16] Evan: Dedicated will be higher fixed cost but lower per-token swings and more predictable unit cost when you have sustained traffic. We'll provide a modeled cost per 1M tokens for both.
[06:26] Ravi: any limits on shard sizes for KV caching for 8k contexts?
[06:31] Samira: 8k contexts are supported but affect memory; you may need model quantization + sharding to fit. We'll test 8k context with int8 and int4 to see memory vs perf tradeoffs.
[06:44] Jordan: do you guys have any blocked items?
[06:46] Ravi: we need the bench, and security docs. If the bench looks good we're open to a pilot.
[06:51] Samira: cool — I'll spin the bench, include cold/warm scenarios, kernel timings, KV hit/miss logs, and quantization deltas. I'll also try a simulated noisy neighbor by launching background noisy clients.
[07:03] Tasha: please record the env and driver versions. We once tried to reproduce and missed a GPU driver mismatch.
[07:09] Samira: yes we will.
[07:11] Jordan: recap — Samira runs bench, Jordan sends security pack, Miguel provides compliance list, Ravi gives traffic profile. Follow-up 2025-04-22.
[07:20] Ravi: thanks everyone, that was useful.
[07:23] Jordan: thanks, we'll share the benchmark link and raw logs.
[07:26] [END]
